newsitem.title: UK: Rightward shift could doom UK Conservatives - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Rightward shift could doom UK Conservatives - Clarke.

text.p: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday that the Conservative party could make itself unelectable if voters perceived it to be drifting further to the anti-European right.
Clarke, one of six candidates to replace John Major as party leader following Labour's landslide election win, gave the warning in a letter to his fellow Conservative MPs.

"I believe firmly that if the Conservative Party is perceived to swing further to the ideological right and also to become hard-line nationalist and anti-European, it will make itself unelectable," Clarke wrote.
Clarke is the most pro-European of the leadership challengers, who include such right wingers as former Welsh Secretary John Redwood and former Home Secretary Michael Howard.
"The British people did not vote for (Labour Prime Minister) Tony Blair because they thought the Conservatives were not sufficiently right-wing or Eurosceptic," Clarke wrote.
"When Blair betrays their trust, many of the moderate voters who have left us could turn to the Liberal Democrats if they believe that the Conservatives have migrated to the hard right of politics."

The 164 Conservative MPs alone will vote on who should replace Major, who announced he would step down immediately the general election result was known. A date for the leadership election has not yet been set. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
